title: OwlsEye: Real-Time Low-Light Video Instance Segmentation on Edge and Exploration of Fixed-Posit Quantization
problem: Video Instance Segmentation (VIS) in low-light conditions on resource-constrained edge devices (autonomous vehicles, surveillance, robotics) is computationally intensive. Existing approaches insufficient for real-time edge deployment.
motivation: Combine model weight quantization, brightness verification, and asynchronous FIFO pipelining with novel Fixed-Posit quantization to enable real-time low-light VIS on embedded systems.
method: YOLOv8 architecture with quantization-based optimization. Techniques: (1) Model weight quantization (INT8, FP32, Fixed-Posit), (2) Brightness verification preprocessing, (3) Asynchronous FIFO pipelining for throughput. Deployed on Intel Nezha embedded platform.
key_novelty: First hardware implementation for real-time VIS in low-light on embedded RGB camera; introduces Fixed-Posit quantization framework (EQyTorch) achieving superior latency/power vs. INT8 and FP32.
contributions: First real-time low-light VIS hardware system on edge device
EQyTorch framework: Fixed-Posit quantization for YOLOv8
Performance improvement: 0.6 FPS → 28 FPS on embedded platform
Fixed-Posit vs. INT8: 2.35x latency, 3.6x power improvement
Fixed-Posit vs. FP32: 9.02x latency, 87.91x power improvement (65nm CMOS)
Synthetic DarkCOCO2017 validation dataset for low-light testing
limitations: Only single platform evaluation (Nezha); power metrics extrapolated for 65nm CMOS (not actual measurement); synthetic dataset may not fully represent real low-light scenarios; no comparison with other edge VIS systems.
primary_theme: Quantization and optimization for edge AI vision
